about: What fifteen AI vendors charge for, read from their own public pages. Each vendor lists the pages read and the exact lines that show what it charges for. watch.mjs re-reads every page and checks each line is still there. First read on 29 October 2026 and checked again on 30 October 2026 for the essay 'From seats to outcomes'.

units.seat: A price per person who has access, whatever they do with it.
units.usage: A price per unit of work the system does: requests, tokens, credits, actions, conversations or sessions.
units.outcome: A price per result the seller counts as a success, such as a resolved conversation or a qualified prospect.
units.accepted-output: A price per piece of work the buyer has checked and accepted.

groups.staff-assistant: Assistants a company's own staff use
groups.customer-agent: Agents that serve a company's customers
groups.my-tools: Tools I pay for myself (an example: replace with yours)

On 15 June 2026 it agreed to buy Fin, formerly Intercom.

vendors.summary: Outcomes: $0.99 per outcome. It was $0.99 per resolution in December 2024; an outcome now also covers a completed handoff, and for its sales agent a disqualified prospect ($0.99) or a qualified one ($9.99), judged against criteria the buyer defines. On other help desks Fin has no seat costs; on Intercom's own, teammates pay per seat. The company now calls itself Fin, and on 15 June 2026 Salesforce agreed to buy it; the pricing pages still say Intercom.

vendors.summary: Resolutions on top of seats: pricing 'primarily seat-based (per agent, per month)', with 5 or 10 automated resolutions included per agent a month, then $1.50 per resolution if committed or $2.00 pay as you go. A language model verifies each resolution before it counts; since 18 May 2026 resolutions are sorted into tiers, and only the verified tier counts against the allowance. A buyer who disagrees with the tier given to a ticket can dispute it through support, and the terms let a buyer dispute the count before the invoice is due.
